title: The production platform for open-weight AI inference
gist: Together AI released a major update to its Dedicated Model Inference platform, adding multiple deployments behind one stable endpoint, canary/blue-green/rolling updates with threshold-based auto-rollback, A/B and shadow traffic testing, multi-signal autoscaling and a Prometheus endpoint, plus a closed beta for full-weight and LoRA reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning. The hard operational disclosures are that Together serves more than 400 trillion tokens per month and that a rebuilt weight caching and distribution layer delivered roughly 4x faster warm starts, with published deployment times from about 2-5 minutes for small models to 7-14 minutes for frontier-scale MoE models.

insights.claim: Together AI says it serves more than 400 trillion tokens per month, and that this operating experience is the basis for its Dedicated Model Inference platform optimizations.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: A rare disclosed throughput figure for a third-party inference provider - useful as a denominator when sizing the open-model serving market.
insights.quote: the lessons we’ve accumulated from serving more than 400 trillion tokens per month
insights.locator: Together Dedicated Model Inference applies the lessons

insights.claim: Model startup time is increasingly dominated by moving hundreds of gigabytes of weights into place as models grow, so Together rebuilt its model caching and distribution layer so weights can be shared across the fleet and proactively warmed before a deployment needs them.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Weight loading, not compute, is the bottleneck for elastic inference capacity - it constrains how quickly any provider can autoscale expensive GPU fleets.
insights.quote: The larger models become, the more startup time is dominated by moving hundreds of gigabytes of weights into place.
insights.locator: Spend less time waiting for models to start

insights.claim: Together reports roughly 4x faster warm starts across several frontier models in internal testing after rebuilding weight caching and distribution.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Faster warm starts directly improve GPU utilization economics for bursty workloads; note this is self-reported internal testing.
insights.quote: In internal testing, this has delivered roughly 4× faster warm starts across several frontier models.
insights.locator: In internal testing, this has delivered

insights.claim: Published average deployment times run about 2-5 minutes for small models such as Qwen 2.5 7B and Llama 3.1 8B, 3-7 minutes for mid-size models such as GPT-OSS 20B, 4-12 minutes for large models such as Llama 3.3 70B and Qwen 3 235B, and 7-14 minutes for frontier-scale MoE models including Kimi K2.7, MiniMax M3, and GLM 5.2.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Concrete cold-start latencies by model class set the practical floor on how responsive open-model autoscaling can be.

themes.theme: Open weights as a control strategy

insights.claim: Together argues open-weight models now match closed models on quality, run at a fraction of the cost, and are fully customizable, making them the foundation for teams building serious AI products and agents.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: The quality-parity claim is the load-bearing assumption behind the entire open-model infrastructure market; it is a vendor claim and should be tested independently.
insights.quote: Open-weight models now match closed models on quality, run at a fraction of the cost, and are fully customizable for your task.
insights.locator: Open-weight models now match closed models on quality

insights.claim: The strategic motivation for adopting open-weight models is the ability to exercise control rather than cost, and many commercial AI applications have adopted a majority open-weight endpoint strategy specifically to maintain complete control over their user experience.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: If control rather than price drives adoption, closed-model vendors cannot defend share by cutting prices - a structurally worse competitive position.
insights.quote: Many commercial AI applications have adopted a majority open-weight endpoint strategy so they can maintain complete control over their user experience.
insights.locator: But the strategic motivation for adopting open-weight models

insights.claim: Many enterprises use open-weight control to incorporate their valuable proprietary IP into models without risking exposure to third parties.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: IP containment is a compliance-grade reason to self-host, which makes open-weight adoption sticky and less price-sensitive than commodity inference.
insights.quote: Many enterprises use this control to incorporate their valuable proprietary IP into models without risking exposure to third parties.

insights.claim: Few teams want to keep aligning a weekly matrix of decisions across quantization levels, parallelism schemes, engine parameters, and draft model architectures even as frontier inference techniques advance just as quickly - the gap Together positions its deployment profiles to fill.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Defines the real product boundary in inference: the value is curated configuration, not raw GPU access - central to whether neoclouds can hold margin.
insights.locator: While open-weight model users want maximum control

insights.claim: An inference endpoint no longer has to map to a single static deployment: multiple deployments with different model weights, hardware, or serving configurations can sit behind the same endpoint so the application never changes how it calls the model.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Decoupling endpoint from deployment is what makes frequent model swapping operationally viable - the mechanism that lowers switching costs between models.
insights.quote: An inference endpoint no longer has to map to a single, static deployment.
insights.locator: Keep the endpoint stable while deployments evolve

insights.claim: The platform supports canary, blue-green, and rolling updates, handling traffic movement and deployment lifecycle while giving the customer control over how quickly a change progresses and when it should stop or roll back.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Standard software release engineering arriving in model serving signals the market maturing from experimentation to regulated production operations.

insights.claim: A/B testing routes a percentage of traffic across deployments for direct comparison while shadow traffic mirrors production requests to a new deployment without affecting the response returned to the user, enabling evaluation on real traffic rather than offline or synthetic benchmarks.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Real-traffic evaluation displaces static benchmarks as the decision input for model selection - a headwind for benchmark-driven marketing.
insights.quote: This makes it possible to evaluate new weights, configurations, and hardware using the traffic that actually matters, rather than relying only on offline benchmarks or synthetic tests.
insights.locator: Test against real traffic without putting users at risk

insights.claim: Autoscaling is not limited to a single generic metric: deployments can scale on inflight requests, GPU utilization, time to first token, latency, decoding speed, or throughput depending on the workload's demand signal.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Multi-signal autoscaling is what lets inference fleets track SLOs rather than raw utilization, improving effective cost per token.
insights.locator: Different workloads have different signals for demand

insights.claim: The platform exposes an organization-level scrapeable Prometheus endpoint so customers can build dashboards, set alerts, monitor rollout health, compare A/B variants, and measure shadow traffic against production in their own observability tooling.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Open observability integration is table stakes for enterprise procurement and reduces lock-in objections.

insights.claim: Customers can deploy models from Together's model platform or bring their own open-weight or fine-tuned model, uploading full model weights or adapters from Hugging Face, S3, or a local machine.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Bring-your-own-weights support is the practical enabler of the open-weight control thesis and the main differentiator versus closed API vendors.
insights.locator: Bring the model you want to serve

insights.claim: Together is opening a closed beta for custom training including full-weight and LoRA reinforcement learning and advanced supervised fine-tuning, configurable through a Python SDK with multiple concurrent LoRA experiments on dedicated capacity.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Moving from serving into RL post-training expands the provider's wallet share and competes directly with hyperscaler training platforms.

insights.claim: Checkpoints from custom training deploy natively into inference deployments with no separate handoff between training and serving and no rebuilding of the setup to move from a post-training experiment to production evaluation.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Closing the train-to-serve loop on one platform is a classic lock-in mechanism; it raises switching costs once customers run RL there.
insights.locator: Custom training connects experimentation directly to production

insights.claim: Decagon's Max Lu says Together already got their latency where it needed to be for voice, and that the new platform changes how they ship model versions - canarying a new fine-tuned model on a small percentage of live traffic with automatic rollback if key metrics regress.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: The only named third-party validation in the post, and the benefit cited is release velocity rather than raw performance.
insights.quote: Together already got our latency where it needed to be for voice.
insights.locator: Max Lu at Decagon described the shift this way

insights.claim: The precision you run, the hardware you deploy on, the serving configuration you use, and the way you scale and route traffic all meaningfully affect performance, reliability, and cost - Together's argument that inference is more than hosting a model behind an API.
insights.speaker: Nikitha Suryadevara, Ted Cui, Will Van Eaton, Charles Zedlewski
insights.so_what: Explains why inference gross margins can differ widely between providers running the same open weights on the same GPUs.
insights.quote: The precision you run, the hardware you deploy on, the serving configuration you use, and the way you scale and route traffic all have a meaningful impact on performance, reliability, and cost.
insights.locator: Delivering that combination of control and simplicity
